It starts with a phone call.
“This is the police. Do not hang up. Tell no one.”
Over six thousand billion dong lost in eleven months of 2025.
And only a third of victims ever report it.
They don’t lack knowledge.
They lack sixty seconds — and someone to ask.
This is Khoan Đã.
Pause. Verify. Protect.
One screen. Four big buttons.
Talk, family, emergency — and one for when someone calls.
Someone is calling? Tap what they are asking you to do.
Two yes-or-no questions. No typing.
A bubble stays on screen, even in other apps.
Only when risk is high, a red strip appears.
Tap once to check what you are looking at.
Your phone asks you to confirm. One picture, never saved.
If a code arrives during a call, Khoan Đã warns you: do not read it out.
No time to tap? Face down for 1.3 seconds, or shake three times.
The rescue screen opens. You choose who to call.
One: split the message and understand it —
who is speaking, and what is being negated.
Two: plain pattern rules — they run even with no AI.
Three: AI reads, and only raises flags.
Each flag carries a quote as evidence.
Four: every quote must match the message — or the flag is dropped.
Five: fixed rules decide.
Fifty-eight signals. Ten critical combinations.
Six: if the input cannot be read, it is never treated as fine.
Seven: the verdict. High risk. Hang up now.
If fear takes over: pause sixty seconds, and say:
“Let me ask my family, and call you back.”
Three labels only. High risk. Suspicious. No clear risk signals found.
Never a fourth.
Family, one tap away. Official bank numbers, with sources.
We expect more people to pause before they transfer,
to be measured in a pilot with older adults.
That protects savings, wellbeing, inclusion, and trust.
571 messages, all written by us.
No real victim messages yet. That is our next step.
